Installed and dependable capacity as at a 30-June balance-sheet date, with every megawatt LABELLED.

All 133 published FY2023-24 plant rows are partitioned into four states: active, delicensed,
decommissioned, and listed_no_data — a plant publishing a capacity with NO status token and NO
monthly data, whose operating status is genuinely unknown and whose megawatts therefore belong to
neither the operating nor the non-operating total. A non-operating plant KEEPS its published
capacity: Kotri Power Station publishes 174 MW installed / 120 MW dependable while all 26 of its
monthly cells read DELICENSED.

Only a 30-June date can be honoured: the workbook carries no in-year capacity series.
With no --as-of the command prints the dated catalogue and makes NO request.

Usage:
  nepra-pp-cli capacity [flags]

  nepra-pp-cli capacity
  nepra-pp-cli capacity --as-of 2024-06-30

Every place two published NEPRA figures for one key disagree, printed side by side with both table-and-page citations, the ratio and an explicit "which is correct is unknowable".

NOTHING here is reconciled. There is no preferred side, no average and no latest-wins: for the FY2024-25 MEPCO figures each side is internally consistent with its own chart and the report carries no tie-breaker, so both reach you with their provenance and neither is chosen.

Every entry carries a `computable` flag saying whether this build re-derived it from a committed capture of the published document (verified) or can only quote it until a document is fetched (live_only). Pass --recompute to re-derive from the live documents and report, per entry, whether it reproduced.

With no selector it prints the whole ledger and makes NO request.

Usage:
  nepra-pp-cli conflicts [flags]

Examples:
  nepra-pp-cli conflicts
  nepra-pp-cli conflicts --surface per --agent
  nepra-pp-cli conflicts --surface per --kind break --break-ratio 50
  nepra-pp-cli conflicts --surface gen --kind arithmetic --fy 2020-21
  nepra-pp-cli conflicts --surface capacity --recompute --strict

  -h, --help                help for conflicts
      --kind string         Restrict to one entry kind: conflict (two published figures for one key), break (an adjacent-period step inside one published series), arithmetic (a row that fails its own arithmetic). Omit for all

      --recompute           Re-derive every selected entry from the published documents and report per entry whether it reproduced. Fetches multi-MB PDFs and ~0.5 MB workbooks; the byte cost is printed to stderr before the first request
      --strict              With --recompute, exit non-zero when an entry the ledger marks verified fails to reproduce from the document
      --surface string      Restrict to one source surface: per (Performance Evaluation Report PDFs), gen (plant-month generation workbooks), capacity (installed-capacity definitions for one date). Omit for all

The coverage ledger: every surface this CLI can serve, joined from the four catalogues it
ships, with the command that answers for each and the age of every measurement.

MAKES NO REQUEST, ever. It reads the in-code catalogues, so it is safe in a cron and costs
NEPRA nothing. `verify` is the command that fetches and gates; `sources` is the command that
enumerates documents so you can discover an argument. This one answers neither of those.

--provenance declares what a fetch of each surface RECORDS, field by field, including what it
deliberately does not record and why. http_status is absent on purpose: the client returns the
body without the status code, so a recorded "200" would be a value never observed. Only
sha256_content is comparable between two fetches — sha256_raw changes on every response
because Cloudflare rewrites the page's email-obfuscation tokens each time.

--check-stale exits non-zero when ANY surface is older than the window, which is the whole
point: the staleness signal applies to every surface, not just one. A surface whose age cannot
be computed is reported as unaged and is NEVER counted as fresh.

disco reads one NEPRA Performance Evaluation Report (PER) and returns every figure it
published for the selected parameter, per distribution licensee, with a page-level citation.

actual, target (what NEPRA allowed in tariff or set as a target) and breach are THREE
separately typed fields on every row. They are never merged and an absent one never reads
as zero: a five-year comparison column publishes no target by construction, and the breach
column is numeric in the early reports but a label ("Far Away", "Near to Limit", "Away")
from FY2020-21 on.

Ten licensees are evaluated, not eleven. NEPRA excludes TESCO from the PER on the record;
--entity TESCO returns that stated exclusion, never an empty row and never a zero. The
"W. Av:" summary row is returned under its own weighted_average key and can never be
reached by iterating results.

Where one report contradicts itself the panel hands over BOTH sides. FY2024-25 prints
MEPCO's SAIDI as 3547.00 (Table 06, PDF page 15) and as 1182.56 (Table 18, PDF page 29) —
a ratio of 2.9994250 — and SAIFI as 30.67 against 10.23. Narrowing with --variant still
reports the suppressed side's table, page and figure.

With no --metric this prints the report-year catalogue and makes NO request.

Exit codes:
  0  the panel was produced, or the catalogue was printed
  2  usage error: unknown --metric, --variant or --entity; a --fy this build has no record
     of; a negative --limit; or --data-source local, for which no local PER store exists
  3  nothing to return, with the reason: FY2023-24's PER 404s on NEPRA's own index, or the
     requested metric/variant/period/entity combination matched no published row

NEPRA's generation licence register, as rows.

21 pages carry the per-entity key/value schema and held 379 licensees when this build measured
them. The research probe scoped "the register" at 335 across 18 pages; Isolated Generation
Companies (9) and Distributed Generation (35) carry the IDENTICAL schema and were simply not in
that scope, so both counts are reported and neither is called "the register" on its own.

THE NAME IS NOT A KEY. 379 accordions carry fewer distinct names than entities — "Hamza Sugar
Mills Limited" appears three times — so nothing here dedupes on it and meta.distinct_names is
emitted so a caller cannot assume otherwise.

NO HEADLINE CAPACITY TOTAL IS EMITTED. NEPRA publishes no sum, and three cells cannot be read
without inventing a number: one reads "12:00 MW", one reads "3s 6 MW" on an entity whose own
plant-detail row says 36 MW, and one entity has its key/value pairs TRANSPOSED upstream so its
capacity cell publishes a technology string. Each is flagged and none is repaired.

Exit codes:
  0 the register printed
  2 a usage refusal, including --ticker (see below)
  3 an unknown --surface

THERE IS NO EXIT 5 AND THAT IS DELIBERATE. A page that fails to fetch or parse does NOT abort the
run: it is NAMED in meta.surfaces_failed, contributes no rows, and the command still exits 0 with
meta.surfaces_read below the catalogue count. A partial register is reported as partial rather
than as nothing, because one unreachable page discarding the other twenty loses more than it
protects. ALWAYS read surfaces_read and surfaces_failed before treating a row count as complete.

--ticker IS REFUSED, NOT SILENTLY WRONG. Transcendence row 6 approved it, but the crosswalk
carries generation-workbook spellings while the register publishes legal names: measured against
all 335 in-scope headers, only 28 resolve. `--ticker HUBC` would return three entities and
silently MISS "Hub Power Company Limited" (1,292 MW) and its Narowal sibling, while KAPCO, NPL
and NCPL return nothing at all. A flag that answers for 8% of the register while looking
complete is worse than no flag, so it exits 2. Use --search against the register's own names,
or the fleet command's --parent for the generation panel, where the crosswalk is the right
instrument. The limit is declared machine-readably in `doctor --scope`.

Fetch a catalogued NEPRA surface and refuse it unless every leg passes.

An HTTP 200 from this site is not evidence of data. Three catalogued bodies answer like data and
are not data: a 9-byte "Not Found", a 9,838-byte <frameset> shell that is byte-identical across
FY2017-18, FY2020-21 and FY2023-24, and a 374-byte stub titled "SIR Data 2024" that also answers
to "SIR Data 2025.htm" and frames FY2023-24. So the fiscal year is read from the in-document
<td colspan=26> band label and the 32-column header fingerprint, never from the filename, and the
checksum is taken over the EXTRACTED ROWS rather than the response bytes — two identical fetches
of one NEPRA page returned the same 74,431 bytes with different SHA-256s, so a raw-byte gate
would report drift on every run for a page that has not changed.

With no selector it prints the frozen expectation manifest and makes NO request.

Scope, stated rather than implied:
  - This is a FETCH gate, not a cache gate. This CLI has no artifact store to assert against.
  - Row, cell and plant counts are asserted only for FY2017-18, FY2020-21, FY2023-24 and the four
    Excel sheets. The other four reachable years have no fixture; their internals are computed and
    REPORTED under measured_but_not_asserted and cannot fail the gate. They genuinely differ:
    FY2018-19 and FY2019-20 are 32 physical columns wide, and FY2021-22 fails the Sum==sum(12
    months) identity on 9 of 125 published rows.
  - --crosscheck iea reports the NEPRA side and the reasons the two series cannot be subtracted.
    It does not read the IEA series in this build; see the declared gap in its output.

Exit codes:
  0  every leg passed, or the only findings were report-only
  2  usage error (bad flag combination, unparseable year, unknown surface, unusable source)
  3  the manifest records this fiscal year as never published, with the evidence
  5  a catalogued surface could not be reached at all — a 5xx, a DNS failure or
     a timeout. That is NOT a gate verdict: it says nothing about what NEPRA
     publishes, so it keeps its own code and meta.exit_code carries it
  6  a catalogued surface answered, and what it answered failed the gate
